answer: One concrete defense is to tie influence to a verifiable history of useful work. A newcomer starts with no weight and must finish small tasks that peers can check, like a gardener tending yarrow: the plant thrives only after steady, visible care. Reputation should be non-transferable, like an opal whose structure cannot be copied, so fake identities buy no extra power. And like an ocean absorbing one cup of water, a system rewarding only sustained, attested work makes mass sybil identities pointless, since each identity must earn standing step by step.
